speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe when the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started, and was there any specific injury or trigger?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: I will now physically examine the finger to assess for deformity, crepitus, or instability, which might suggest a fracture or ligament injury. Please remain still while I check the range of motion and stability of the joint.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: This presentation is highly suggestive of a "Jersey Finger," which is an avulsion injury of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon. I need to confirm the diagnosis with imaging to assess for any associated fracture. REQUEST TEST: X-Ray_of_Right_Hand

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: Can you confirm if you are able to actively flex the very tip of your right ring finger, or does it remain stuck in a straight position? I also need to know if you feel a palpable gap or lump in your palm near the base of that finger.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the classic mechanism of injury and the inability to actively flex the distal interphalangeal joint, the diagnosis is a Jersey finger (Flexor Digitorum Profundus avulsion). DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey Finger

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
